materialization_gate: Do not build or inject the broken starter from this topology until an independent creation controller approves it against the clean A2A architecture.

topology_summary.intent: A small number of shared lifecycle defects should fan out across several resource families. The solver should repair common production logic rather than patch tests or ten unrelated implementations.

root_cause_clusters.RC1_STATE_IDENTITY: The common lifecycle state layer derives or publishes identity and applied state from mutable plan data instead of a stable external object key and the last successful transition.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_REFRESH_RECONCILIATION: Read is not a true observation path: it reuses prior Terraform state and, on some branches, routes through Ansible mutation helpers rather than native Linux observers.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_UPDATE_TRANSACTION: Update advances Terraform state or decides no work is required before the Ansible mutation has durably succeeded, so retries and source-driven updates become incorrect.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_DELETE_FAILURE: Delete treats requested teardown as completed before independently establishing successful or already-absent external state, and resource-specific removal selectors are not sufficiently scoped.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_RUNNER_COMMAND: The shared Ansible runner constructs commands through shell-oriented text, weakly handles process outcomes, and does not own timeout/cancellation/temp-file cleanup as one transaction.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_NORMALIZATION_IDEMPOTENCY: Desired and observed values use inconsistent canonical forms for unordered maps, modes/ownership, and cron defaults, creating false diffs and unnecessary mutations.

defects.observable: A successful Create can return a resource whose Terraform state has an empty or missing stable id.
Changing mutable directory mode or symlink target changes resource identity even though the external object key is unchanged.
Computed observed values are reconstructed from transient process data instead of the applied Terraform state and disappear after provider restart.
After successful copy creation the destination digest is not persisted consistently, so a fresh process cannot establish the same applied state.
Apply followed by a new Terraform process produces identity/state churn on an otherwise unchanged managed object.
Externally deleting a managed directory is not detected by terraform plan or refresh.
External mode drift on a file or directory is echoed as the prior value instead of refreshed from the target.
Changing a managed symlink to point at a different target is not reported as drift.
Out-of-band modification of ansibleops_copy destination content is not reflected in refreshed state.
Out-of-band changes to a managed user's shell or supplementary groups are not detected.
A clean plan or refresh invokes ansible-playbook and increments the verifier's execution counter even when no mutation is required.
Update publishes the planned values before ansible-playbook finishes successfully.
An intentionally failed Update leaves Terraform state claiming the new desired configuration rather than the previous successful configuration.
Retry after a failed Update can be skipped because the prematurely advanced state makes the desired configuration appear already applied.
Changing source_digest does not reliably execute one copy update and publish the resulting destination digest.
Changing a managed line can append a second line or execute repeatedly instead of replacing the named line contract exactly once.
Delete clears the logical resource before the Ansible teardown result is known.
When Ansible deletion is forced to fail, Terraform nevertheless finishes destroy as though the resource were gone.
Deleting one named line, block, or cron resource can remove a sibling managed entry because the removal selector is scoped only by the backing file or user.
Destroy removes a managed user's home even when remove_home_on_destroy is false, or preserves it when the option is true.
The runner assembles ansible-playbook through sh -c or equivalent shell text, allowing shell metacharacters in input to be interpreted.
Valid source, destination, or temporary paths containing spaces are split incorrectly and fail execution.
A non-zero ansible-playbook exit can be reported as a successful lifecycle transition.
Context cancellation or timeout does not reliably terminate the Ansible child process and is not returned as a failed transition.
Generated temporary playbooks remain after success, failure, or timeout and accumulate across Terraform runs.
Equivalent template vars supplied in different map insertion orders produce unstable rendered task payloads or false updates.
Equivalent file modes or owner/group representations compare unequal and cause a perpetual plan diff after successful apply.
Omitted cron schedule fields and explicit wildcard defaults normalize differently, causing repeated updates on an otherwise unchanged cron resource.

partial_fix_traps: Fixing individual resource Read methods without repairing the shared observation/refresh path leaves sibling drift and side-effect failures.
Suppressing state diffs without correcting native observation can make plans appear clean while external state remains wrong.
Checking ansible-playbook exit status alone is insufficient if Update already advanced Terraform state before execution.
Escaping a few shell characters is insufficient; the runner must stop using shell interpretation and pass argv/data structurally.
Sorting template variables alone does not fix mode, ownership, or cron canonicalization.
Special-casing failed destroy in one resource leaves the shared delete transaction and sibling selectors incorrect.

provider_contract: exact ten resources are exposed through Terraform provider schema
forbidden null_resource/terraform_data/provisioner substitutes cannot satisfy lifecycle tests
create_and_state: first apply executes expected Ansible mutation
stable id and applied attributes persist in real Terraform state
new Terraform/provider process observes the same resource identity
refresh_and_drift: external deletion, mode drift, content drift, symlink drift, and user drift are detected through Read
update_transaction: failed update retains prior successful state and retry converges
delete_transaction: successful delete removes only the owned external object and Terraform state
runner_safety: spaces and shell metacharacters remain literal
non-zero exit, timeout, and cancellation fail safely
idempotency: unordered maps and canonical defaults do not create perpetual diffs
repeated plan and refresh do not replay Ansible

next_gate.on_approval: Materialize the already-designed clean provider and inject only defects represented by this approved topology.
